STEP 1 - Scene: This looks like a steak (medium-rare sirloin or flank-style beef) cut into pieces on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near top-down angle. The plate sits on top of another white tray with QR-code printing, which is not part of the meal.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square white dish, roughly 22 cm across its width (a side plate-sized vessel). Area ≈ 22 × 22 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Three pieces of beef steak (two larger slices, one smaller piece), a few small green herb flecks (parsley or chives, negligible), and a light oil/juice sheen on the plate.

STEP 4 - Area: Beef pieces together cover roughly 15% of the plate (about 60 cm²). Herbs and oil sheen are under 1% and ~2% respectively. Total food-covered area ≈ 17%, consistent with the visible scatter.

STEP 5 - Volume: Beef pile height is about 1.2 cm on average (pieces are thin slices, ~1–1.5 cm thick). 60 cm² × 1.2 cm ≈ 72 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Meat bulk density ~0.95 g/ml → beef ≈ 68 g. Oil/juice sheen ≈ 2 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked beef steak (lean-medium, with some fat) ≈ 230 kcal/100 g → 68 g ≈ 156 kcal. Oil/juice ≈ 2 g × 880 kcal/100 g ≈ 18 kcal (oil fraction, small). Herbs negligible (~1 kcal).

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three modest steak pieces on a side-plate-sized dish at ~70 g and ~175 kcal is plausible for what is visible; it is not a full serving, just the remaining portion.

Total: about 70 g, about 175 kcal.
